summary: Orange County's two-story wooden Bolero lookout, built in 1946, was demolished in March 1989; no source we read describes the site today.

notes_for_editor: History is well sourced and consistent: FFLOS (built 1946, removed 1989), the LA Times (March 16, 1989, Wednesday demolition) and Forest Lookouts (March 15, 1989) agree. No source describes the site today, so no access level is recorded. The OC Parks listing title suggests a hike route to the lookout, but the listing text we fetched carries no description, so verify before adding access. Elevation disagrees: the Times gives Bolero Peak as 1,600 feet, the FFLOS record gives the site as 1,756 ft (535 m), and the record's 535.2 m is kept. Agency: FFLOS and the Times say Orange County or its Fire Department; Forest Lookouts places the site in Cleveland National Forest, which may describe the land rather than the owner. The LA Times line that the structures were built by state prison work crews refers to the lookouts generally; Bolero is not named in that sentence. The staffing 'unstaffed' value rests on 'not used for over a decade' (Forest Lookouts, 1989).
